name: Snapcase
label: Victory Records
lede: A West Seneca basement band cut its first single with Goo Goo Doll Robby Takac, made a 1997 record Turnstile and Drug Church still name, and quit in 2005 when it got tough to keep flogging a dead horse.

eras.title: A basement in West Seneca
eras.text: Four Buffalo-suburb teenagers, the youngest 15, started Solid State and went through singers and drummers across four demos. By 1992 they were Snapcase, signed to Victory, with the bassist at the mic.

years.cap: Daryl Taberski on bass at the River Rock Cafe, Buffalo, 1989
years.h: Solid State starts in a West Seneca basement
years.p: Guitarist Scott Dressler is 15, drummer Mike Kimaid 17, bassist Daryl Taberski 18 and singer Tiger Balduf 19. The band that becomes Snapcase starts outside Buffalo.

years.h: Solid State records Quest for Reality with a new singer and drummer
years.p: Tiger Balduf and Mike Kimaid are gone before the tape rolls, so Chris Galas sings and Peter Dawidzik drums.
years.xp:
Balduf left to get married and Kimaid left to join the Watchmen.

On May 22, 1990 a second demo, Accept Your Fate, was recorded with friend Mike Lampe: Galas, Dressler, Taberski and Jason Kourkounis on drums.

years.h: Joe Smith of the Watchmen adds a second guitar and the name changes
years.p: Jason Kourkounis leaves and Kimaid comes back on drums. The five-piece is now Snapcase.
years.xp: Two more demos followed with Dennis Fura, Break the Silence and King of the Mountain, recorded across 1991 and 1992.

years.h: Goo Goo Dolls bassist Robby Takac helps record Snapcase's first 7"
years.p: Chicago's Victory Records signs the band. Comatose is recorded with Mike Sac and Takac, from Buffalo's Goo Goo Dolls.
years.xp:
Joe Smith's guitar harmonics were the record's sound. Daryl Taberski later said people were really into it, "so we continued to build around that component."

Maximum Rocknroll's review called it a "flute sound", which amused the band.

years.h: Daryl Taberski picks up the mic as Chris Galas leaves
years.p: After the Comatose single Taberski moves from bass to vocals. Bob Whiteside and Jon Salemi arrive from the Buffalo band Support, on bass and guitar.
years.xp:
Taberski has called himself not a good bassist, and says friends told him he should sing since he was already talking into the mic and doing backup vocals.

Galas stayed his best friend. They patched things up after some initial tension.

eras.title: A first album, a lost drummer, a label package tour
eras.text: Snapcase made Lookinglasself with Don Fury, lost its drummer mid-session and found his replacement in Slugfest, the Buffalo band Scott Vogel co-founded. By 1996 it was sharing a stage and a live album with Earth Crisis and Strife.

years.h: A drummer quits mid-session and a Slugfest man finishes Lookinglasself
years.p: Snapcase's first album is recorded with Don Fury and Fred Betschen. Mike Kimaid leaves partway, and Timothy Redmond, formerly of Slugfest, plays the rest.
years.xp:
Scott Vogel formed Slugfest in the early 90s with his stepbrother Jay, and the band put out Buried Alive in 1993. Vogel later fronted [[Terror|697eba1a-bf52-46b1-a19f-4d7190b63e5c]].

Redmond's move to Snapcase ended Slugfest bar a few reunion shows. He stayed Snapcase's drummer until 2002.

years.h: Victory's Only the Strong compilation puts Fields of Illusion beside Strife
years.p: The label's 1993 comp carries the Snapcase track next to [[Strife|5e911223-4228-4a14-8f6c-7d2dfeb62530]] and the rest of Victory's early roster.

years.h: Dressler's last record is the Steps EP
years.p: Fred Betschen records it in early 1995. Dressler had been in the band since the basement.

years.h: Scott Dressler leaves for grad school and Frank Vicario steps in
years.p: Dressler later becomes an economics professor at Villanova University. Vicario comes over from Fadeaway, another Buffalo band.
years.xp: Taberski says Vicario showed up at his first rehearsal with the riff to Caboose. After Vicario's first show, Dressler told him "That 'Caboose' song is the best Snapcase song."

years.cap: Snapcase at the original California Takeover, Whisky a Go Go, Hollywood, April 1996
years.h: Victory records Snapcase, Earth Crisis and Strife live at the Whisky
years.p: A Hollywood night at Whisky a Go Go becomes the live album The California Takeover, released that summer.
years.xp:
The April 1996 shows also included the Showcase Theatre in Corona. Dave Jagosz engineered the live record.

Strife's Andrew Kline: "The Whisky was not ready for a real hardcore show, and people were getting kicked out left and right." Victory owner Tony Brummel came with a fever.

eras.title: Two weeks and a case of chickenpox
eras.text: Progression Through Unlearning was recorded fast, sick and young, and barely reviewed. It's now the record Turnstile, Higher Power and Drug Church name, and it took the band onto Warped Tour and Deftones bills.

years.cap: Snapcase at the Mercury Theatre, Buffalo, 1997
years.src: Wikipedia: Progression Through Unlearning · Wikipedia: Snapcase
years.h: Progression Through Unlearning goes down in two weeks, chickenpox and all
years.p: Steve Evetts produces at Trax East in New Jersey in January 1997, with guitarist Jon Salemi playing sick. A decade later the band said the recording and mastering were rushed.
years.xp:
Few outlets reviewed it at the time. Vice's Dan Ozzi called it a "timeless hardcore classic" in 2017, and Wikipedia credits it with pointing toward 2000s metalcore and the melodic hardcore revival, with Turnstile, Higher Power and Drug Church citing it.

The album has 11 tracks and runs 32:25. Salemi remembers the sessions as "very, very quick." Killing Yourself to Live and Vent were co-written with the departed Dressler.

years.h: Snapcase spends the summer of 1997 on the Vans Warped Tour
years.p: The band carries Progression Through Unlearning onto Warped, then takes the fall off so members can go to school.

years.cap: Snapcase with Millencolin and Samiam in Japan
years.h: Deftones crowds meet Snapcase on the fall 1998 tour with Quicksand
years.p: Snapcase opens for Deftones and [[Quicksand|3c9f8bef-a658-4204-9ee8-7e95d2535b32]], and cuts [[Bad Brains|e919b253-da5b-4aae-a444-6a368376a2d6]]' I with Brian McTernan for the tribute Never Give In.
years.xp:
Taberski on opening big rooms: "You're playing when people are still coming through the door." Small hardcore shows, he says, stayed more memorable.

He also recalls a meeting with Tommy Boy Records founder Tom Silverman, who asked about BPM and floated a "Snapcase backpack." The band laughed about it afterward.

years.h: Bob Whiteside leaves after a split 7" with Boysetsfire
years.p: Energy Dome backs [[Boysetsfire|ba561cc7-2050-47d3-8bc2-c645a1393d90]]'s Truth Hits Everybody. Dustin Perry, from Minnesota's Threadbare, takes over on bass.

years.h: Snapcase headlines Hellfest in Syracuse
years.p: The hardcore festival puts the Buffalo band at the top of its bill in summer 1999, two years after Progression Through Unlearning.

eras.title: Warped's main stage, then a dead horse
eras.text: Snapcase moved onto Warped's main stage and a European tour with NOFX while the hardcore crowd that loved Progression drifted. By late 2004 the band called it.

years.h: Steve Evetts returns for Designs for Automotion
years.p: The third album is recorded in summer 1999 and comes out in January 2000.

years.h: Snapcase tours Europe with NOFX, then takes Warped's main stage
years.p: The trip is the Deconstruction tour with [[NOFX|dcaa4f81-bfb7-44eb-8594-4e74f004b6e4]]. Back home, the Vans Warped Tour gives the band a main-stage slot.

years.h: Ben Lythberg takes the drum stool while Timothy Redmond finishes a master's
years.p: Lythberg covers from fall 2000 to spring 2001, and later becomes the permanent drummer.

years.h: Toonami scores its Mobile Fighter G Gundam promos with Snapcase
years.p: Cartoon Network's Toonami block uses Breaking and Reaching.

years.h: Brian McTernan records End Transmission at Salad Days Studios
years.p: It's Snapcase's fourth album. Afterwards Timothy Redmond leaves for good and Ben Lythberg becomes the drummer.

years.h: Snapcase hits the road with Boysetsfire and a young Atreyu
years.p: [[Atreyu|17e137fb-59e5-4fd7-af48-afc34995396c]] is then one of Victory Records' rising metalcore bands, and [[Boysetsfire|ba561cc7-2050-47d3-8bc2-c645a1393d90]] is on the same bill.

years.h: Bright Flashes collects covers of Helmet, Devo and Jane's Addiction
years.p: Snapcase's last release also holds remixes and songs from the End Transmission concept.
years.xp: Earlier that year Snapcase opened for Bad Religion and Finch on its last trip abroad.

q: tough to keep flogging a dead horse when hearts are in other places
years.h: Frank Vicario tells fans why Snapcase is breaking up
years.p: The band's statement says its popularity has been waning for a few years. Vicario adds that fans came to the newer records with fixed ideas of what Snapcase should sound like.
years.xp:
Punknews ran the news with a farewell show promised for January in Buffalo. Some members started a project called Ourselves.

The last two records were End Transmission (2002) and Bright Flashes (2003).

years.h: The last show in Buffalo brings back almost every former member
years.p: Timothy Redmond, Scott Dressler and Bob Whiteside play, and original singer Chris Galas joins for Comatose.
years.xp:
Afterwards Redmond taught AP Government and Global History at Williamsville East High School, and Dressler became an assistant professor of economics at Villanova University.

Vicario, Perry and Lythberg formed the band Attractive with Josh English of Sixgoingonseven.

eras.title: Buffalo keeps calling them back
eras.text: Snapcase never settled back in for good, but it kept returning for benefits, anniversaries and hometown shows. A volcano grounded one comeback, and the 25th birthday went to the Town Ballroom.

years.h: Snapcase plays Mohawk Place in Buffalo for the first time since 2005
years.p: Two nights at Brooklyn's Music Hall of Williamsburg follow on November 24 and 25.
years.xp: The Brooklyn shows were a benefit for Callum Robbins and doubled as the release party for the Anti-Matter Anthology book.

years.h: Eyjafjallajökull's ash cloud cancels Snapcase's April return to Europe
years.p: Flights are grounded and the April dates go with them, Belgium's Groezrock among them. The band reschedules for July.
years.xp: The band said on Twitter that rebooking could take three weeks.

years.h: Snapcase and Sick of It All play a hometown reunion in Buffalo
years.p: [[Sick of It All|e204ed91-3684-4561-b29b-d0b53f8459a7]] shares the bill. Chicago's Riot Fest and Austin's Fun Fun Fun Fest follow later in 2010.
years.xp: Frank Vicario had said the band had "no intention of doing an extended reunion beyond the European and Buffalo, New York, shows."

years.h: Sick of It All asks Snapcase to play its 25th anniversary at Webster Hall
years.p: The March 26 show is in New York, with Snapcase in the support slot.

years.h: Snapcase plays the tenth This Is Hardcore at Union Transfer
years.p: The Philadelphia festival films the full set.

years.cap: Snapcase at Tune Inn, New Haven
years.h: Buffalo's Town Ballroom hosts Snapcase's birthday party
years.p: Twenty-five years after Solid State became Snapcase, the band celebrates at home.

years.h: Twenty-five years later, The Return of the California Takeover
years.p: Snapcase, [[Earth Crisis|88a6037e-87ba-492a-a54c-c927aa620cb8]] and [[Strife|5e911223-4228-4a14-8f6c-7d2dfeb62530]] share a record again, with the same three-band billing as 1996.

yt: Caboose at Town Ballroom, Buffalo, Feb 8, 2025
years.h: Snapcase takes on Refused's Summer Holidays vs. Punkroutine
years.p: The cover is for the tribute The Shape of Punk to Come Obliterated. Snapcase also plays Far Out, Bro on And Now I'm Just Gnashing My Teeth.

q: we wouldn't exist as a band if it wasn't for them
yt: Official trailer, 4 Decades of Uncompromising Hardcore documentary
years.h: Zero Tolerance gets a Snapcase cover for a shelter benefit
years.p: Snapcase records Back to Square One for Iodine Recordings' The Dogs of Hope. Daryl Taberski calls Zero Tolerance the forefathers of Buffalo hardcore.
years.xp:
Taberski: "Zero Tolerance are considered the forefathers of Buffalo hardcore and we wouldn't exist as a band if it wasn't for them."

Net profits go to the Randolph County Animal Shelter in Wedowee, Alabama, a no-kill facility. The record comes out August 1 and also carries tracks by Killswitch Engage, Deadguy and Orange 9mm.
